title.zh: 卷一百十四 志第六十七 禮十七
title.raw: 卷一百十四 志第六十七 禮十七 Volume 114 Treatises 67: Rites 17

sentences.zh: 禮十七

translations.literal: Rites Seventeen
translations.idiomatic: Rites Seventeen

sentences.zh: （嘉禮五）〉

translations.literal: (Ceremonial Rites Five)
translations.idiomatic: (Ceremonial Rites, Part Five)

sentences.zh: ○巡幸養老視學賜進士宴幸秘書省進書儀大射儀鄉飲酒禮

translations.literal: ○ Imperial tours; nourishing the aged; viewing the schools; banquets for granting jinshi; banquets at imperial visits to the Directorate of Archives; procedures for presenting books; great archery ceremony; village drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Imperial tours; nurturing the elderly; inspecting the schools; banquets for newly minted jinshi; banquets during imperial visits to the Directorate of Archives; procedures for presenting books; the great archery ceremony; and the village drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 巡幸之制，唐《開元禮》有告至、肆覲、考制度之儀，《開寶通禮》因之。

translations.literal: As for regulations for imperial tours, the Tang Kaiyuan Rites had protocols for announcing arrival, paying homage, and examining institutions; the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for imperial tours were set out in the Tang dynasty's Kaiyuan Rites, which prescribed ceremonies for announcing the emperor's arrival, receiving homage, and reviewing local institutions; the Song Kaibao Comprehensive Rites adopted these same protocols.

sentences.zh: 太祖幸西京，所過賜夏、秋田租之半。

translations.literal: When Taizu visited the Western Capital, along the route he granted half of the summer and autumn land tax.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu toured the Western Capital, he halved the summer and autumn land rents for every district he passed through.

sentences.zh: 真宗朝諸陵及舉大禮，途中皆服折上巾、窄袍，出京、過京城，服靴袍、具鸞駕。

translations.literal: In the Zhenzong reign, when visiting the imperial tombs or performing great ceremonies, on the road all wore folded-up caps and narrow robes; when leaving the capital or passing through the capital, they wore boot-robes and arranged the imperial palanquin escort.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenzong, whenever the court visited the imperial tombs or held a major ceremony, the emperor wore a folded cap and close-fitting robe while still on the road; only when he left the capital or entered it did he don state boots and robes and take up the full imperial palanquin escort.

sentences.zh: 群臣公服係鞋，供奉班及內朝官前導。

translations.literal: The various ministers wore official dress with tied shoes; the attendance corps and inner-court officials led the way.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers wore court dress with tied shoes, while the attendance corps and inner-court officials went ahead as guides.

sentences.zh: 凡從官並日赴行宮，合班起居，晚朝視事，群臣不赴。

translations.literal: All accompanying officials daily went to the traveling palace, assembled in formation for greetings, and held evening audiences to handle affairs; the various ministers did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: All accompanying officials reported daily to the traveling palace, where they formed ranks to greet the emperor and held evening audiences to conduct state business; the rest of the ministry did not attend.

sentences.zh: 中頓侍食，百官就宿頓迎駕訖，先發，或道途隘遠，則免迎駕。

translations.literal: At midday halts they attended meals; when officials at the overnight halt had finished welcoming the imperial progress, they set out first; if the road was narrow or remote, welcoming the progress was waived.
translations.idiomatic: At midday halts the emperor dined, and officials at the next overnight station, once they had finished welcoming the procession, set out ahead; if the route was narrow or remote, the welcoming ceremony was omitted.

sentences.zh: 將進發，近臣、諸軍賜裝錢。

translations.literal: When about to set out, close attendants and the various armies were granted travel allowance money.
translations.idiomatic: Before departure, the emperor's close attendants and the various military units received travel stipends.

sentences.zh: 出京，留司馬、步諸軍夾道左右，至新城門外奉辭，留守辭於門內，百官、父老辭於苑前，召留守等賜飲苑中。

translations.literal: On leaving the capital, the capital commandant and infantry troops lined both sides of the road; at the outer gate of the New City they offered farewells; the acting governor took leave inside the gate; officials and elders took leave before the imperial park; the acting governor and others were summoned and granted drink in the park.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving the capital, the capital commandant and infantry lined both sides of the road. At the outer New City gate they bade farewell; the acting governor did so inside the gate, while officials and local elders did so before the imperial park. The acting governor and his staff were then summoned and treated to wine in the park.

sentences.zh: 州縣長吏、留司官待於境。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county chief officials and acting capital officials waited at the border.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county magistrates and officials left behind in the capital waited at the border to receive him.

sentences.zh: 所過賜巡警兵、守津梁行郵治道卒時服錢履，父老綾袍、茶帛，途中賜衛士緡錢。

translations.literal: Along the route he granted patrol troops, ferry and postal road maintenance soldiers seasonal clothing, money, and shoes; to elders, damask robes, tea, and silk; along the road he granted guardsmen strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route he gave patrol troops, ferry guards, postal couriers, and road maintenance workers seasonal clothing, cash, and shoes; to local elders he gave damask robes, tea, and silk; and to his guards he distributed strings of cash along the way.

sentences.zh: 所幸寺、觀，賜道、釋茶帛，或加紫衣、師號。

translations.literal: At temples and monasteries visited, he granted Daoist and Buddhist clergy tea and silk, or additionally purple robes and master titles.
translations.idiomatic: At temples and monasteries he visited, he bestowed tea and silk on Daoist and Buddhist clergy, and sometimes added purple robes and honorific master titles.

sentences.zh: 吏民有以饔餼、酒果、方物獻者，計值答之。

translations.literal: When officials and commoners presented cooked food, wine, fruit, or local products, he calculated their value and reciprocated.
translations.idiomatic: When officials or commoners presented food, wine, fruit, or local products, he paid them back at assessed value.

sentences.zh: 命官籍所過係囚、逋負者，日引對，多原釋。

translations.literal: He ordered officials to register prisoners and debtors along the route; daily he summoned them for audience, and mostly pardoned and released them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials to register prisoners and debtors in each district he passed through, then summoned them daily for audience and, in most cases, pardoned and released them.

sentences.zh: 仍采訪民間疾苦，振恤鰥、寡、孤、獨。

translations.literal: He also inquired into the people's hardships and provided relief to widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary.
translations.idiomatic: He also inquired into popular hardships and provided relief to widowers, widows, orphans, and those living alone.

sentences.zh: 車服、度量、權衡有不如法，則舉儀制禁之。

translations.literal: Where carriage dress, measures, or weights and balances were not in accord with regulations, he cited ritual statutes to prohibit them.
translations.idiomatic: Where carriage insignia, dress, measures, or weights and balances failed to meet the code, he invoked ritual regulations to forbid them.

sentences.zh: 有奇材、異德及政事尤異者，孝子、順孫、義夫、節婦為鄉里所稱者，其不守廉隅、昧於正理者，並條析以聞。

translations.literal: Those of extraordinary talent or virtue and those whose governance was especially outstanding; filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives praised by their villages; and those who did not uphold integrity or were ignorant of proper principle—all were itemized and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Men of extraordinary talent or virtue, officials whose governance stood out, filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives praised in their communities, as well as those who lacked integrity or failed to grasp proper conduct—all were catalogued and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 官吏知民間疾苦者，亦許錄奏。

translations.literal: Officials who knew of the people's hardships were also permitted to record and memorialize them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who were aware of popular hardships were also allowed to submit written reports.

sentences.zh: 所過州、府，結彩為樓，陳音樂百戲。

translations.literal: At every prefecture and superior prefecture passed, they erected festooned towers and staged music and variety performances.
translations.idiomatic: In every prefecture and superior prefecture along the route, people erected decorated towers and staged music and variety shows.

sentences.zh: 道、釋以威儀奉迎者，悉有賜。

translations.literal: Daoist and Buddhist clergy who welcomed him with full ritual deportment all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist and Buddhist clergy who welcomed him with full ceremonial pomp all received rewards.

sentences.zh: 東京留守遣官表請還京，優詔答之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital acting governor dispatched an official with a memorial requesting return to the capital; an edict of gracious reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The acting governor of the Eastern Capital sent an official with a memorial asking the emperor to return; the court answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 駕還京，大陳兵衛以入。

translations.literal: When the imperial progress returned to the capital, a great array of military guards was deployed for entry.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, the emperor entered with a full display of military guards.

sentences.zh: 凡行幸，太祖、太宗不常其數。

translations.literal: As for imperial tours in general, Taizu and Taizong did not keep them to a fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu and Taizong, imperial tours were not held on any fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 自咸平中，車駕每出，金吾將軍帥士二百人，執楇周繞，謂之禁圍，春、夏緋衣，秋、冬紫衣。

translations.literal: From the Xianping era onward, whenever the imperial carriage went out, the Jinwu general led two hundred soldiers bearing staffs to encircle it, called the forbidden perimeter; in spring and summer, scarlet robes; in autumn and winter, purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xianping era on, whenever the emperor went out, the Jinwu general led two hundred soldiers with staffs to form a cordon around the carriage—the "forbidden perimeter"—wearing scarlet in spring and summer and purple in autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 郊祀、省方並增二百，服錦襖，出京師則加執劍。

translations.literal: For suburban sacrifices and provincial tours alike, two hundred more were added; they wore brocade jackets; when leaving the capital, swords were added.
translations.idiomatic: For suburban sacrifices and provincial tours, another two hundred men were added, dressed in brocade jackets; when leaving the capital they also carried swords.

sentences.zh: 親王、中書、樞密、宣徽行圍內，餘官圍外。

translations.literal: Imperial princes, the Secretariat, Military Affairs Commission, and Palace Service walked inside the perimeter; other officials outside it.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and the heads of the Secretariat, Military Affairs Commission, and Palace Service walked inside the cordon; all other officials walked outside it.

sentences.zh: 大禮備儀衛，則有司先布土為黃道，自宮至祀所，左右設香台、畫甕、青繩闌干。

translations.literal: When great ceremonies deployed full guards of honor, the relevant offices first laid earth to form a yellow path from the palace to the sacrificial site; on both sides they set incense platforms, painted urns, and blue-rope railings.
translations.idiomatic: For major ceremonies with full ceremonial guards, the relevant offices first laid out an earthen "yellow path" from the palace to the sacrificial site, flanked by incense platforms, painted urns, and blue-rope railings.

sentences.zh: （巡省在途則不設。）〉

translations.literal: (On provincial tours while on the road, these were not set up.)
translations.idiomatic: (On provincial tours while still on the road, these were not set up.)

sentences.zh: 凡巡省，翰林進號傳詩付樞密院，每夕摘字，令衛士相應為識。

translations.literal: For all provincial tours, the Hanlin submitted numbered transmitted poems to the Military Affairs Commission; each evening a character was selected, and guardsmen were made to respond in correspondence as identification.
translations.idiomatic: On every provincial tour, the Hanlin Academy submitted numbered cipher poems to the Military Affairs Commission; each evening a character was chosen, and guardsmen had to respond with the matching sign as identification.

sentences.zh: 東京舊城城門、西京皇城司並契勘，內外城、宮廟門並勘箭，出入皆然。

translations.literal: The gates of the Eastern Capital old city and the Western Capital imperial city office all kept tally records; inner and outer city gates and palace and temple gates all checked tally arrows; entry and exit were alike.
translations.idiomatic: The gates of the Eastern Capital's old city and the Western Capital imperial city office all kept tally records; gates of the inner and outer cities and of palaces and temples all verified tally arrows on entry and exit alike.

sentences.zh: 入藩鎮外城、子城門亦勘箭。

translations.literal: Entering a prefectural outer city or inner city gate also required tally-arrow verification.
translations.idiomatic: Entry through a prefectural outer or inner city gate likewise required tally-arrow verification.

sentences.zh: 朝陵定扈從官人數，入柏城者，僕射以上三人，丞、郎以上二人，餘各一人。

translations.literal: For tomb visits the number of accompanying officials was fixed; those entering the cypress enclosure: three or more at the rank of vice director and above, two at the rank of assistant director and above, one each for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: For visits to the imperial tombs, the number of attendants was fixed: three officials of vice director rank or above, two of assistant director rank or above, and one each for all others might enter the cypress enclosure.

sentences.zh: 東封，定仗內導駕官從人數，親王、中書、樞密、宣徽、三司使四人，學士、尚書丞郎、節度使三人，大兩省、大卿監、三司副使、樞密承旨、客省閣門使副、金吾大將軍押仗鳴珂、內殿崇班以上二人，餘各一人。

translations.literal: For the Eastern Fengshan, the number of officials within the guard formation who guided the imperial carriage was fixed: imperial princes, Secretariat, Military Affairs, Palace Service, and Three Departments commissioners—four each; academicians, Secretariat vice directors, and military commissioners—three each; grand secretaries of both provinces, grand directors, Three Departments vice commissioners, Military Affairs commissioners, Reception Bureau and Gate Bureau commissioners and vice commissioners, Jinwu great generals escorting the guard with jade clappers, and inner palace honor guards and above—two each; one each for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: For the eastern Fengshan rite, the number of officials in the inner escort who guided the imperial carriage was fixed: four each for imperial princes and the heads of the Secretariat, Military Affairs Commission, Palace Service, and Three Departments; three each for Hanlin academicians, Secretariat vice directors, and military commissioners; two each for grand secretaries of both provinces, grand directors, Three Departments vice commissioners, Military Affairs commissioners, Reception and Gate Bureau commissioners and deputies, Jinwu great generals escorting the guard with jade clappers, and inner-palace honor guards and above; and one each for all others.

sentences.zh: 命諸司巡察之。

translations.literal: He ordered the various offices to inspect and patrol them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the relevant offices to inspect and enforce compliance.

sentences.zh: 自後舉大禮，皆循此制。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever great ceremonies were held, all followed this system.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, every major ceremony followed this same system.

sentences.zh: 三年，幸杭州，自杭州幸江寧府，尋幸浙西，自浙西幸浙東。

translations.literal: In the third year, he visited Hangzhou; from Hangzhou he visited Jiangning Prefecture; soon after he visited western Zhejiang; from western Zhejiang he visited eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he toured Hangzhou, then from Hangzhou to Jiangning Prefecture, then soon afterward to western Zhejiang, and from there to eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：“國家遭金人侵逼，無歲無兵。

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued, saying: "The state has suffered Jin invasion and coercion; not a year passes without warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "Our state has suffered invasion and coercion by the Jin; not a year passes without war.

sentences.zh: 朕纂承以來，深軫念慮，謂父兄在難，而吾民未撫，不欲使之陷於鋒鏑。

translations.literal: Since I succeeded to the throne, I have deeply brooded in concern, thinking that while father and elder brothers are in peril, yet our people are not yet pacified, and I do not wish to let them fall into spear and blade.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne I have brooded deeply on this, thinking that while my father and elder brother remain in peril, my people are still unrested, and I do not wish to see them fall to spear and blade.

sentences.zh: 故包羞忍恥，為退避之謀，冀其逞志而歸，稍得休息。

translations.literal: Therefore I swallowed shame and endured humiliation, adopting a strategy of withdrawal, hoping that they might satisfy their will and return, so that we might gain a little rest.
translations.idiomatic: So I swallowed shame and endured humiliation, adopting a strategy of retreat in the hope that they might satisfy their ambitions and withdraw, giving us a little respite.

sentences.zh: 自南京移淮甸，自淮甸移建康而會稽，播遷之遠，極於海隅。

translations.literal: From Nanjing we moved to the Huai region, from the Huai region to Jiankang and then Kuaiji; the distance of our wanderings reached the sea's edge.
translations.idiomatic: We moved from Nanjing to the Huai region, from the Huai region to Jiankang and then to Kuaiji; our flight has carried us to the very edge of the sea.

sentences.zh: 卑詞厚禮，使介相望。

translations.literal: With humble words and lavish gifts, envoys followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: With humble words and lavish gifts, our envoys followed one upon another without pause.

sentences.zh: 以至願去尊稱，甘心貶屈，請用正朔，比於藩臣，遣使哀祈，無不曲盡。

translations.literal: To the point of wishing to relinquish honorific titles, willingly accepting degradation, requesting use of their calendar, comparing ourselves to vassal ministers—dispatching envoys in tearful supplication, nothing was left unexhausted in bending.
translations.idiomatic: We were willing to relinquish our honorific titles, accept degradation, adopt their calendar, and rank ourselves as vassal ministers; we sent envoys in tearful supplication and bent ourselves in every way imaginable.

sentences.zh: 假使金石無情，亦當少動。

translations.literal: Even if metal and stone were without feeling, they ought to have been moved a little.
translations.idiomatic: Even metal and stone ought to have been moved a little.

sentences.zh: 累年卑屈，卒未見從。

translations.literal: Years of humble submission, yet in the end they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Years of humble submission have won us nothing in return.

sentences.zh: 生民嗷嗷，何時寧息？

translations.literal: The living people cry out in distress—when will there be peace?
translations.idiomatic: The people cry out in distress—when will they know peace?

sentences.zh: 今諸路之兵聚於江、浙之間，朕不憚親行，據其要害。

translations.literal: Now the armies of the various circuits are gathered between the Yangzi and Zhejiang; I do not shrink from going in person to hold the strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Now the armies of every circuit are gathered between the Yangzi and Zhejiang; I do not shrink from going in person to hold the strategic points myself.

sentences.zh: 如金人尚容朕為汝兵民之主，則朕於事大之禮，敢有不恭！

translations.literal: If the Jin still permit me to be your lord over soldiers and people, then in the rites of serving the greater power, how would I dare be disrespectful!
translations.idiomatic: If the Jin are still willing to let me remain your sovereign over soldiers and people, then in the rites of serving a greater power, how could I dare be disrespectful!

sentences.zh: 或必用兵窺我行在，傾我宗社，塗炭生靈，竭取東西金帛、子女，則朕亦何愛一身，不臨行陣，以踐前言，以保群生。

translations.literal: Or if they must use troops to spy on my traveling palace, overturn our altars of state, reduce the living to charcoal, and exhaust all gold, silk, and sons and daughters east and west—then what would I cherish of my single person, not to go to the battle line, to fulfill my earlier words, and to preserve the multitude of lives?
translations.idiomatic: But if they insist on sending troops against my traveling palace, overturn our altars of state, reduce the people to ruin, and strip us of all gold, silk, sons, and daughters from east to west—then what would I cherish of my own life? I will not fail to take the field, to keep my earlier pledge, and to preserve the lives of the people.

sentences.zh: 朕已取十一月二十五日移蹕，前去浙西，為迎敵計。

translations.literal: I have set the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month to move the imperial progress, proceeding to western Zhejiang to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I have set the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month to move the court westward into Zhejiang to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 惟我將士人民，念國家涵養之恩，二聖拘縻之辱，悼殺戮焚殘之禍。

translations.literal: Only my generals, soldiers, and people—think on the state's nurturing grace, the humiliation of the two emperors held captive, and mourn the calamity of slaughter, burning, and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: My generals, soldiers, and people: remember the nurturing grace of the state, the humiliation of our two captive emperors, and mourn the calamity of slaughter, burning, and ruin.

sentences.zh: 與其束手待斃，曷若並計合謀，同心戮力，奮勵而前，以存家國！

translations.literal: Rather than binding your hands and waiting to perish, how much better to join plans and unite counsel, with one heart and combined strength, to rouse yourselves and advance, thereby preserving family and state!
translations.idiomatic: Rather than waiting with bound hands to die, join your plans, unite your strength, rouse yourselves, and advance together to preserve our family and state!

sentences.zh: ”乃詔御前應奉官司自合扈從外，內太常寺據實用人數扈從，餘接續起發。

translations.literal: " Then it was decreed that, apart from the Imperial Front Service offices that were to accompany as appropriate, within this the Directorate of Ritual Music was to accompany according to actual personnel numbers needed; the rest were to set out in succession.
translations.idiomatic: " He then decreed that, apart from the Imperial Front Service offices that were to accompany as appropriate, the Directorate of Ritual Music should accompany with only the personnel actually required, while the rest were to set out in succession.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，次台州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, he halted at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he halted at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，次溫州。

translations.literal: In the second month, he halted at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he halted at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，幸浙西。

translations.literal: In the third month, he visited western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he toured western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，詔移蹕臨安府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, an edict moved the imperial progress to Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing, an edict moved the court to Lin'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔周視軍師，車駕進發，遣官奏告天地、社稷、宗廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered a comprehensive inspection of the armies; the imperial carriage set out, and officials were dispatched to report to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict ordered a comprehensive inspection of the armies; the emperor set out, and officials were dispatched to report to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 自臨安幸平江，尋幸建康。

translations.literal: From Lin'an he visited Pingjiang; soon after he visited Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: From Lin'an he toured Pingjiang, and soon afterward Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，還臨安。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year, he returned to Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he returned to Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 三十一年九月，詔：“金人背盟失信，今率精兵百萬，躬行天討，用十二月十日車駕進發，應行宮臨安府文武百僚城北奉辭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirty-first year, an edict said: "The Jin have betrayed the alliance and broken faith; now leading a million elite troops, I personally undertake Heaven's punitive campaign; on the tenth day of the twelfth month the imperial carriage will set out; all civil and military officials of the traveling palace at Lin'an Prefecture shall offer farewell north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirty-first year an edict declared: "The Jin have betrayed the alliance and broken faith. I now lead a million elite troops to undertake Heaven's punitive campaign in person. On the tenth day of the twelfth month the imperial carriage will set out, and all civil and military officials of the traveling palace at Lin'an shall bid farewell north of the city.

sentences.zh: ”其日，應文武百僚先詣城北幕次，俟車駕御舟將至，御史台、閣門、太常寺分引文武百僚立班定，兩拜訖，俟御舟過，班退。

translations.literal: " On that day, all civil and military officials first went to the tent compound north of the city; when the imperial carriage in its boat was about to arrive, the Censorate, Gate Bureau, and Directorate of Ritual Music separately led the civil and military officials to form ranks; after two bows were completed, they waited until the imperial boat had passed, then the ranks withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " On that day all civil and military officials first went to the tent compound north of the city. When the emperor's boat was about to arrive, the Censorate, Gate Bureau, and Directorate of Ritual Music led the officials into formation; after two bows they waited until the imperial boat had passed, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三十二年正月，詔：“視師江上，北騎遁去，兩淮無警，已委重臣統護諸將經畫進討。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirty-second year, an edict said: "In inspecting the armies on the Yangzi, the northern horsemen have fled; the two Huai regions are without alarm; I have already entrusted important ministers to oversee the generals and plan the advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirty-second year an edict said: "While inspecting the armies on the Yangzi, the northern cavalry have fled and the two Huai regions are secure. I have entrusted senior ministers to oversee the generals and plan the advance.

sentences.zh: 今暫還臨安，畢恭文祔廟之禮。

translations.literal: Now I temporarily return to Lin'an to complete the rites of reverent enshrinement of Emperor Gongwen in the collateral temple.
translations.idiomatic: I now return temporarily to Lin'an to complete the rites of enshrining Emperor Gongwen in the collateral temple.

sentences.zh: 宜令有司增修建康百官吏舍、諸軍營砦，以備往來巡幸，可擇日進發。

translations.literal: The relevant offices should be ordered to expand and build the official quarters of the hundred officials at Jiankang and the various army camps and stockades, to prepare for coming and going on tours; a day may be chosen to set out.
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices expand the official quarters and army camps at Jiankang to prepare for future tours, and choose a day to set out when ready.

sentences.zh: ”車駕還宮。

translations.literal: " The imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 養老於太學，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，乘金輅，至太學酌獻文宣王。

translations.literal: Nourishing the aged at the Imperial Academy: the emperor wore the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, rode the golden carriage, and arrived at the Imperial Academy to pour libation and offer sacrifice to King Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: To nurture the elderly at the Imperial Academy, the emperor wore the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, rode the golden carriage, and arrived at the academy to pour libation and offer sacrifice to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 三祭酒，再拜，歸御幄。

translations.literal: The three libationers each bowed twice and returned to the imperial canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The three libationers each bowed twice and returned to the imperial canopy.

sentences.zh: 比車駕初出，量時刻，遣使迎三老、五更於其第。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage first set out, judging the time, envoys were sent to welcome the Three Elders and Five Watchmen at their residences.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the imperial carriage set out, envoys were dispatched at the appointed time to welcome the Three Elders and Five Watchmen at their homes.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更俱服朝服，乘安車，導從至太學就次；

translations.literal: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen all wore court dress, rode secure carriages, and with guides and attendants arrived at the Imperial Academy and took their places;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen all wore court dress, rode secure carriages, and with escorts arrived at the Imperial Academy and took their stations;

sentences.zh: 國老、庶老，有司預戒之，各服朝服，集於其次。

translations.literal: the State Elders and Common Elders, whom the relevant offices had warned in advance, each wore court dress and assembled at their stations.
translations.idiomatic: the State Elders and Common Elders, whom the relevant offices had notified in advance, each wore court dress and assembled at their stations.

sentences.zh: 大樂正帥工人、二舞入，立於庭。

translations.literal: The grand music director led the musicians and the two dance troupes in; they stood in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The grand director of music led the musicians and both dance troupes into the courtyard and took their positions.

sentences.zh: 東上閣門、御史台、太常寺、客省、四方館自下分引百官、宗室、客使、學生等，以次入就位，如視學班。

translations.literal: The Eastern Upper Gate Bureau, Censorate, Directorate of Ritual Music, Reception Bureau, and Four Directions Office from below separately led officials, imperial clansmen, guest envoys, students, and others to enter in order and take their places, as in the school-inspection formation.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Upper Gate Bureau, Censorate, Directorate of Ritual Music, Reception Bureau, and Four Directions Office led officials, imperial clansmen, guest envoys, students, and others in turn to their places, following the same formation used when inspecting the schools.

sentences.zh: 太常博士讚三老、五更俱出次，引國老、庶老立於後，重行異位。

translations.literal: The Ritual Music academician intoned that the Three Elders and Five Watchmen should all leave their stations; he led the State Elders and Common Elders to stand behind them, in double rows at separate positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Music academician announced that the Three Elders and Five Watchmen should leave their stations, then led the State Elders and Common Elders to stand behind them in double rows at separate positions.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人引左輔奏請中嚴，少頃，又奏外辦，皇帝出大次，侍衛如常儀。

translations.literal: The ritual duty officer and the communications chamberlain led the left assistant to memorialize requesting inner solemnity; after a short while, they again memorialized that the outer preparations were complete; the emperor came out of the great tent; the guard of honor followed the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led the left assistant to request inner solemnity; shortly afterward they reported that outer preparations were complete, and the emperor emerged from the great tent with guards of honor following the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 大樂正令撞黃鍾之鍾，右五鍾皆應，協律郎跪，俯伏，舉麾興，宮架《乾安之樂》作，皇帝即御坐，樂止。

translations.literal: The grand music director ordered the striking of the yellow bell; the five bells to the right all responded; the pitch regulator knelt, prostrated himself, raised the baton and signaled rise; the palace orchestra performed the Qian'an music; the emperor then took the imperial seat; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The grand director of music ordered the yellow bell struck; the five bells to the right answered in turn; the pitch regulator knelt, prostrated himself, raised his baton to signal the rise, and the palace orchestra performed the Qian'an music as the emperor took his seat; then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰“再拜”，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies said "Bow twice"; all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies called "Bow twice," and all officials in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更杖而入，各左右二人夾扶，太常博士前引，史臣執筆以從。

translations.literal: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen entered leaning on staffs; on each side two men supported them; the Ritual Music academician led in front; historiographers followed holding brushes.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen entered leaning on staffs, each supported by two attendants on either side, led by the Ritual Music academician while historiographers followed with brushes in hand.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更入門，宮架《和安之樂》作，至宮架北，北向立，以東為上。

translations.literal: When the Three Elders and Five Watchmen entered the gate, the palace orchestra performed the He'an music; arriving north of the palace orchestra, they stood facing north, with east as the superior position.
translations.idiomatic: As the Three Elders and Five Watchmen entered the gate, the palace orchestra played the He'an music; they halted north of the orchestra, faced north, and took position with the east as the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎引群老隨入，位於其後，樂止。

translations.literal: The ritual attendant led the assembly of elders to follow in; they took positions behind them; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual attendants led the assembly of elders in behind them; the music then ceased.

sentences.zh: 博士揖進，三老在前，五更在後，仍杖夾扶，宮架《和安之樂》作，至西階下，樂止。

translations.literal: The academician bowed and advanced; the Three Elders in front, the Five Watchmen behind, still supported by staffs on both sides; the palace orchestra performed the He'an music; arriving below the western steps, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The academician bowed and led them forward, the Three Elders ahead and the Five Watchmen behind, still supported on their staffs, while the palace orchestra played the He'an music until they reached the foot of the western steps, where the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 博士揖三老、五更自西階升堂，國老、庶老立堂下。

translations.literal: The academician bowed and the Three Elders and Five Watchmen ascended the hall by the western steps; the State Elders and Common Elders stood below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The academician bowed, and the Three Elders and Five Watchmen ascended the hall by the western steps while the State Elders and Common Elders remained below.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更當御坐揖，群老亦揖，皇帝為興。

translations.literal: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen, facing the imperial seat, bowed; the assembly of elders also bowed; the emperor rose in response.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the imperial seat, the Three Elders and Five Watchmen bowed, as did the assembly of elders, and the emperor rose in response.

sentences.zh: 次奉禮郎揖國老升堂，博士引三老、五更，奉禮郎引國老以下，各於席後立。

translations.literal: Next the ritual attendant bowed and the State Elders ascended the hall; the academician led the Three Elders and Five Watchmen; the ritual attendant led the State Elders and those below; each stood behind his mat.
translations.idiomatic: Next ritual attendants bowed the State Elders up the hall; the academician led the Three Elders and Five Watchmen, while attendants led the State Elders and those below, each taking position behind his mat.

sentences.zh: 典儀讚各就坐，讚者承傳，宮架《尊安之樂》作，三老、五更就坐。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies intoned that each should take his seat; the intoner transmitted it; the palace orchestra performed the Zun'an music; the Three Elders and Five Watchmen took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies announced that each should take his seat, the announcement was relayed, the palace orchestra played the Zun'an music, and the Three Elders and Five Watchmen sat down.

sentences.zh: 三公授幾、九卿正履訖，殿中監、尚食奉御進珍羞及黍稷等，先詣御坐前進呈，遂設於三老前，樂止。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies presented armrests; the Nine Ministers straightened their shoes; the palace director and the imperial food service commissioner advanced delicacies and millet and glutinous grain; first they presented before the imperial seat, then set them before the Three Elders; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies presented armrests; the Nine Ministers adjusted their footwear; the palace director and imperial food commissioner brought delicacies, millet, and glutinous grain, first presenting them before the imperial seat and then setting them before the Three Elders; the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 尚食奉御詣三老坐前，執醬而饋訖。

translations.literal: The imperial food service commissioner went before the Three Elders' seats, held the sauce, and completed the feeding.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial food commissioner went before the Three Elders' seats, held the sauce, and completed the feeding ceremony.

sentences.zh: 尚醞奉御詣酒尊所，取爵酌酒，奉御執爵，奉於三老。

translations.literal: The imperial wine service commissioner went to the wine vessel place, took the goblet and poured wine; the commissioner held the goblet and presented it to the Three Elders.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial wine commissioner went to the wine vessels, filled a goblet, and presented it to the Three Elders.

sentences.zh: 次太官、良醞令以次進珍羞酒食於五更、群老之前，皆食。

translations.literal: Next the grand provisioner and fine wine commissioner in order advanced delicacies and wine and food before the Five Watchmen and assembly of elders; all ate.
translations.idiomatic: Next the grand provisioner and fine-wine commissioner in turn set delicacies, wine, and food before the Five Watchmen and the assembly of elders, and all ate.

sentences.zh: 大樂正引工人升，登歌奏《惠安之樂》，三終。

translations.literal: The grand music director led the musicians up; the elevated song performed the Hui'an music, three times to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The grand director of music led the musicians up, and the elevated chorus performed the Hui'an music three times through.

sentences.zh: 史臣既錄三老所論善言、善行，宮架作《申安之樂》。

translations.literal: Once the historiographers had recorded the good words and good deeds discussed by the Three Elders, the palace orchestra performed the Shen'an music.
translations.idiomatic: After the historiographers had recorded the good words and good deeds offered by the Three Elders, the palace orchestra performed the Shen'an music.

sentences.zh: 《憲言成福之舞》畢，文舞退，作《受成告功之舞》，畢，三老以下降筵，博士引三老、五更於堂下，當御坐前，奉禮郎引群老復位，俱揖，皇帝為興。

translations.literal: When the Xianyan chengfu dance was finished, the civil dancers withdrew; the Shoucheng gaogong dance was performed; when finished, the Three Elders and below descended from the mats; the academician led the Three Elders and Five Watchmen below the hall, before the imperial seat; the ritual attendant led the assembly of elders back to position; all bowed; the emperor rose in response.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianyan chengfu dance ended, the civil dancers withdrew and the Shoucheng gaogong dance was performed. When it ended, the Three Elders and those below left their mats; the academician led the Three Elders and Five Watchmen below the hall before the imperial seat; ritual attendants led the assembly of elders back into position; all bowed, and the emperor rose in response.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更降階至堂下，宮架《和安之樂》作，出門，樂止。

translations.literal: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen descended the steps to below the hall; the palace orchestra performed the He'an music; they went out the gate; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen descended to the foot of the hall while the palace orchestra played the He'an music; they went out through the gate, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人引左輔前奏禮畢，退，復位。

translations.literal: The ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led the left assistant forward to memorialize that the rites were complete; they withdrew and returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led the left assistant forward to announce that the rites were complete, then withdrew to their positions.

sentences.zh: 典儀讚拜訖，皇帝降坐，太常卿導還大次，百僚以次退，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies intoned that the bows were complete; the emperor descended from the seat; the Director of Ritual Music led him back to the great tent; the hundred officials withdrew in order; the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies announced that the bows were complete; the emperor left his seat; the Director of Ritual Music led him back to the great tent; officials withdrew in order; and the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更升安車，導從還，翼日詣闕表謝。

translations.literal: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen mounted secure carriages; with guides and attendants they returned; the next day they went to the palace gate to present thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elders and Five Watchmen mounted their secure carriages and returned with their escorts; the next day they came to the palace gate to present their thanks.

sentences.zh: 視學。

translations.literal: Viewing the schools.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the schools.

sentences.zh: 哲宗始視學，遂幸國子監，詣至聖文宣王殿行釋奠禮，一獻再拜。

translations.literal: When Zhezong first inspected the schools, he then visited the Directorate of Education, went to the Hall of the Sagely King Wenxuan to perform the libation ceremony, one offering and two bows.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong first inspected the schools, he visited the Directorate of Education and went to the Hall of the Sagely King Wenxuan to perform the libation ceremony with one offering and two bows.

sentences.zh: 御敦化堂，召從官賜坐，禮部、太常寺、本監官承事郎以上侍立，承務郎以下、三學生坐於東西廡，侍講吳安詩執經，祭酒豐稷講《尚書》《無逸》終篇，復命宰臣以下至三學生坐，賜茶，豐稷賜三品服，本監官、學官等賜帛有差。

translations.literal: He proceeded to the Dunhua Hall, summoned attending officials and granted them seats; Ministry of Rites, Directorate of Ritual Music, and directorate officials of rank Assistant Director and above stood in attendance; Assistant Section Member and below and students of the three schools sat in the eastern and western corridors; lecturing attendant Wu Anshi held the classic; libationer Feng Ji lectured through the final chapter of the Documents "Against Dissipation"; he then ordered the chief ministers down to the three-school students to sit, granted tea; Feng Ji was granted third-rank robes; directorate officials, school officials, and others were granted silk in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeded to the Dunhua Hall and summoned his attendants to sit. Officials of the Ministry of Rites, Directorate of Ritual Music, and the directorate at the rank of Assistant Director and above stood in attendance, while those below that rank and students of the three schools sat in the eastern and western corridors. Lecturing attendant Wu Anshi held the classic while libationer Feng Ji lectured through the final chapter of the Documents' "Against Dissipation." The emperor then ordered the chief ministers and students to sit and granted tea; Feng Ji received third-rank robes, and directorate and school officials received silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 遂幸昭烈武成王廟，酌獻肅揖。

translations.literal: He then visited the Temple of the Illustrious Martial King Wucheng, poured libation and offered sacrifice with a solemn bow.
translations.idiomatic: He then visited the Temple of the Illustrious Martial King Wucheng, poured libation, and offered sacrifice with a solemn bow.

sentences.zh: 徽宗幸太學，遂幸辟雍，奠獻如上儀。

translations.literal: Huizong visited the Imperial Academy, then visited the Piyong, offering libation and sacrifice according to the above protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong visited the Imperial Academy and then the Piyong, offering libation and sacrifice according to the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 詔司業吳絪等轉官改秩，循資賜章服，文武學生授官，免省試、文解，賜帛有差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Director Wu Yin and others to transfer offices and change ranks; according to qualifications they were granted robes and insignia; civil and military students were granted offices, exempted from provincial examination and civil qualifying examination, and granted silk in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Vice Director Wu Yin and others, granted robes and insignia according to qualification, appointed civil and military students to office, exempted them from the provincial examination and civil qualifying examination, and granted silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 所司預設次於敦化堂後，又於堂上稍北當中兩間設次，南向設御坐。

translations.literal: The relevant offices beforehand set up the tent behind the Dunhua Hall; also on the hall slightly to the north, in the central two bays, they set up the tent; facing south they set the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices set up the imperial tent behind the Dunhua Hall and in the two central bays slightly north on the hall floor, with the imperial seat facing south.

sentences.zh: 又設從官及講筵講書、執經官並太學官坐御坐之南，東西重行異位。

translations.literal: They also set seats for attending officials and lecture-hall lecturers, classic-holders, and Imperial Academy officials south of the imperial seat, in double rows east and west at separate positions.
translations.idiomatic: Seats were also arranged south of the imperial seat for attending officials, lecturers, classic-holders, and Imperial Academy officials in double rows east and west.

sentences.zh: 太學生坐於兩廡，相向並北上。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy students sat in the two corridors, facing each other and aligned toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy students sat in the two corridors, facing one another and aligned toward the north.

sentences.zh: 宰臣以下從官之次，設於中門外。

translations.literal: The stations for chief ministers and attending officials below them were set outside the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: Stations for the chief ministers and their attendants were set outside the central gate.

sentences.zh: 皇帝酌獻文宣王畢，幸太學，降輦入次，簾垂更衣。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished pouring libation to King Wenxuan, he visited the Imperial Academy, descended from the carriage and entered the tent; the curtain was lowered for changing dress.
translations.idiomatic: After pouring libation to King Wenxuan, the emperor visited the Imperial Academy, descended from his carriage into the tent, and changed dress behind lowered curtains.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人引講官與侍立官入就堂下，皆係鞋。

translations.literal: The ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led the lecturers and standing attendants in to take position below the hall; all tied their shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led lecturers and standing attendants to their positions below the hall, all with tied shoes.

sentences.zh: 講書、執經官、學生各立堂下，東西相向。

translations.literal: Lecturers, classic-holders, and students each stood below the hall, facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturers, classic-holders, and students each stood below the hall, facing one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 俟報班齊，皇帝升坐，班首奏萬福，在位者皆應喏訖，閣門使承旨臨階宣升堂，通事舍人喝拜，應在位者再拜訖，分左右升堂，各就位少立。

translations.literal: When it was reported that the ranks were complete, the emperor ascended to the seat; the rank leader memorialized "Ten thousand blessings"; all in attendance responded "Yes" and finished; the Gate Bureau commissioner, receiving the edict, announced from the steps permission to ascend the hall; the communications chamberlain called for bows; those who should be in attendance bowed twice and finished; they ascended the hall left and right, each took position and stood briefly.
translations.idiomatic: When the ranks were reported complete, the emperor took his seat. The rank leader called "Ten thousand blessings," and all in attendance answered. The Gate Bureau commissioner announced from the steps that they might ascend the hall; the communications chamberlain called for bows; those present bowed twice, then ascended left and right and took their positions.

sentences.zh: 起居郎、舍人分左右侍立。

translations.literal: The attendance recorder and chamberlain stood in attendance left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The attendance recorder and chamberlain stood in attendance to left and right.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人引講書及執經官就北向位，班首奏萬福，閣門使宣升堂，舍人喝再拜訖，分東西升堂，立於御坐左右。

translations.literal: The ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led the lecturers and classic-holders to the north-facing positions; the rank leader memorialized "Ten thousand blessings"; the Gate Bureau commissioner announced ascent to the hall; the chamberlain called for two bows and finished; they ascended the hall east and west separately and stood left and right of the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led lecturers and classic-holders to north-facing positions. The rank leader called "Ten thousand blessings," the Gate Bureau commissioner announced they might ascend, and the chamberlain called for two bows. They then ascended east and west and stood to either side of the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 講書官在西，東向；

translations.literal: the lecturer was on the west, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: The lecturer stood on the west, facing east;

sentences.zh: 執經官在東，西向；

translations.literal: the classic-holder was on the east, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: the classic-holder on the east, facing west;

sentences.zh: 學生就北向位。

translations.literal: the students took north-facing positions.
translations.idiomatic: and the students took north-facing positions.

sentences.zh: 舍人喝拜，在位者皆再拜，立於東西兩廡。

translations.literal: The chamberlain called for bows; all in attendance bowed twice and stood in the eastern and western corridors.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain called for bows; all present bowed twice and stood in the eastern and western corridors.

sentences.zh: 內侍進書案，以經授執經官，稍前，進於案上。

translations.literal: The inner attendant advanced the book desk, handed the classic to the classic-holder, who stepped slightly forward and placed it on the desk.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant brought the book desk, handed the classic to the classic-holder, who stepped forward and placed it on the desk.

sentences.zh: 舍人喝拜就坐，宰臣以下並堂上坐，如閣門所進坐位圖。

translations.literal: The chamberlain called for bows and taking seats; the chief ministers and below all sat in the hall, according to the seating chart submitted by the Gate Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain called for bows and seating; the chief ministers and others sat in the hall according to the seating chart submitted by the Gate Bureau.

sentences.zh: 講書畢，通事舍人曰“可起”，群臣皆起，降階立。

translations.literal: When the lecture was finished, the communications chamberlain said "You may rise"; the various ministers all rose and descended the steps to stand.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture ended, the communications chamberlain said "You may rise," and the ministers all rose and descended the steps to stand.

sentences.zh: 執經官降，講書官於御坐前致辭訖，亦降。

translations.literal: The classic-holder descended; the lecturer, before the imperial seat, delivered closing remarks and finished, then also descended.
translations.idiomatic: The classic-holder descended; the lecturer delivered closing remarks before the imperial seat and then descended as well.

sentences.zh: 舍人喝拜，如有宣答，即再喝拜。

translations.literal: The chamberlain called for bows; if there was an edict response, he again called for bows.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain called for bows, and if there was an imperial response, called for bows again.

sentences.zh: 閣門宣坐賜茶，舍人喝拜訖，宰臣以下升堂，各立於位後，學生各就北向位。

translations.literal: The Gate Bureau announced seating and granting of tea; the chamberlain called for bows and finished; the chief ministers and below ascended the hall, each standing behind his seat; students each took north-facing positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Bureau announced seating and the granting of tea. After bows, the chief ministers ascended the hall and stood behind their seats while students took north-facing positions.

sentences.zh: 舍人喝拜，在位者俱拜訖，各分東西廡，以北為上下。

translations.literal: The chamberlain called for bows; all in attendance bowed and finished; each divided into the eastern and western corridors, with north as superior and south as inferior.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain called for bows; all present bowed, then divided into the eastern and western corridors with north as the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 舍人喝就坐，上下皆就坐。

translations.literal: The chamberlain called to take seats; superiors and inferiors all took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain called them to sit, and all took their seats.

sentences.zh: 賜茶畢，禮直官、通事舍人引堂上官降階就位，舍人喝拜，在位者俱拜訖，禮直官引之以次出。

translations.literal: When the granting of tea was finished, the ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led the hall officials down the steps to take position; the chamberlain called for bows; all in attendance bowed and finished; the ritual duty officer led them out in order.
translations.idiomatic: When tea had been served, the ritual duty officer and communications chamberlain led hall officials down the steps. After bows, the ritual duty officer led them out in order.

sentences.zh: 學生就位，舍人喝拜，學生俱再拜，退。

translations.literal: The students took position; the chamberlain called for bows; the students all bowed twice and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The students took their positions; the chamberlain called for bows; the students all bowed twice and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年七月，國學大成殿告成，奉安廟像。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, the Dacheng Hall of the National University was completed; temple images were installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, the Dacheng Hall of the National University was completed and temple images were installed.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，國子司業高閌請幸學，上從之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, National University Vice Director Gao Kan requested an imperial visit to the school; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, National University Vice Director Gao Kan requested an imperial visit to the school, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔略曰：“偃革息民，恢儒建學。

translations.literal: An edict in summary said: "Lay aside weapons and give the people rest; restore Confucian learning and establish schools.
translations.idiomatic: An edict in summary said: "Lay aside weapons and give the people rest; restore Confucian learning and establish schools.

sentences.zh: 聲明丕闡，輪奐一新。

translations.literal: Our reputation and teachings are greatly unfolded; the halls are wholly renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Our reputation and teachings shine forth anew, and the halls have been wholly renewed.

sentences.zh: 請既方堅，理宜從欲。

translations.literal: The request is already firmly made; by principle I ought to follow your wish.
translations.idiomatic: Your request is earnest, and it is only right that I grant it.

sentences.zh: 將款謁於先聖，仍備舉於舊章。

translations.literal: I shall pay a sincere visit to the former Sage, and still fully perform the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: I shall pay a sincere visit to the former Sage and perform the ceremonies according to the old regulations.

sentences.zh: ”三月，上服靴袍，乘輦入監，止輦於大成殿門外。

translations.literal: " In the third month, the emperor wore boot-robes, rode the palanquin into the directorate, and halted the palanquin outside the Dacheng Hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month the emperor wore boot-robes, rode his palanquin into the directorate, and halted outside the Dacheng Hall gate.

sentences.zh: 入幄，群臣列班於庭。

translations.literal: He entered the tent; the various ministers formed ranks in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the tent while ministers formed ranks in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 帝出幄，升東階，跪上香，執爵三祭酒，再拜，群臣皆再拜，上降入幄。

translations.literal: The emperor came out of the tent, ascended the eastern steps, knelt and offered incense, held the goblet and thrice poured libation, bowed twice; the various ministers all bowed twice; the emperor descended and re-entered the tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerged, ascended the eastern steps, knelt to offer incense, poured libation three times from the goblet, and bowed twice; the ministers all bowed twice, and the emperor returned to the tent.

sentences.zh: 分奠從祀如常儀。

translations.literal: Distributed offerings to collateral sacrifices followed the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Distributed offerings to collateral sacrifices followed the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 尚舍先設次於崇化堂之後，及堂上之中南向設御坐。

translations.literal: The Palace Provisioners beforehand set up the tent behind the Chonghua Hall, and on the hall in the center, facing south, set the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Provisioners set up the imperial tent behind the Chonghua Hall and placed the imperial seat in the center of the hall facing south.

sentences.zh: 閣門設群臣班於堂下，如月朔視朝之儀。

translations.literal: The Gate Bureau set the ranks of the various ministers below the hall, as in the protocol for the first-of-month court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Bureau arranged the ministers' ranks below the hall as at the first-of-month court audience.

sentences.zh: 宰輔、從臣次於中門之外。

translations.literal: Chief ministers and attending officials had their stations outside the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers and attending officials waited outside the central gate.

sentences.zh: 上乘輦幸太學，降輦於堂，入次更衣。

translations.literal: The emperor rode the palanquin to visit the Imperial Academy, descended from the palanquin at the hall, entered the tent to change dress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode to the Imperial Academy, descended at the hall, and changed dress in the tent.

sentences.zh: 講官入就堂下講位，北向；

translations.literal: the lecturer entered and took the lecture position below the hall, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: The lecturer took the lecture position below the hall, facing north;

sentences.zh: 執經官、學生皆立於堂下，東西相向。

translations.literal: the classic-holder and students all stood below the hall, facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: the classic-holder and students stood below the hall, facing one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 帝出次，升御坐，群臣起居如儀。

translations.literal: The emperor came out of the tent, ascended to the imperial seat; the various ministers performed greetings according to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerged and took his seat; the ministers greeted him according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 乃命三公、宰輔以下升堂，皆就位，左右史侍立。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Three Excellencies, chief ministers, and below to ascend the hall; all took their positions; the left and right historiographers stood in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Three Excellencies, chief ministers, and others to ascend the hall and take their positions, with the left and right historiographers standing in attendance.

sentences.zh: 講書及執經官北面起居再拜，皆命之升立於御坐左右。

translations.literal: The lecturers and classic-holders, facing north, performed greetings and bowed twice; all were ordered to ascend and stand left and right of the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The lecturers and classic-holders, facing north, greeted him and bowed twice, then were ordered to ascend and stand to either side of the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 學生北面再拜，分立兩廡北上。

translations.literal: The students, facing north, bowed twice and divided to stand in the two corridors toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: The students bowed twice facing north and divided to stand in the two corridors toward the north.

sentences.zh: 內侍進書案牙簽，以經授執經官，賜三公、宰輔以下坐。

translations.literal: The inner attendant advanced the book desk with ivory tally slips, handed the classic to the classic-holder, and granted the Three Excellencies, chief ministers, and below permission to sit.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant brought the book desk with ivory tally slips and handed the classic to the classic-holder; the Three Excellencies, chief ministers, and others were granted seats.

sentences.zh: 講畢，群臣皆起，降階，東西相向立。

translations.literal: When the lecture was finished, the various ministers all rose, descended the steps, and stood facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture ended, the ministers all rose, descended the steps, and stood facing one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 執經官降，講官進前致詞，乃降，皆北面再拜，左右史降。

translations.literal: The classic-holder descended; the lecturer advanced to deliver closing remarks, then descended; all faced north and bowed twice; the left and right historiographers descended.
translations.idiomatic: The classic-holder descended; the lecturer advanced to deliver closing remarks and descended; all bowed twice facing north, and the left and right historiographers descended.

sentences.zh: 乃賜茶，三公以下北面再拜，升，各立於位後。

translations.literal: Then tea was granted; the Three Excellencies and below, facing north, bowed twice, ascended, and each stood behind his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Tea was then granted; the Three Excellencies and others bowed twice facing north, ascended, and stood behind their seats.

sentences.zh: 學生北面再拜，分兩廡立，上下就坐。

translations.literal: The students, facing north, bowed twice, divided to stand in the two corridors, and superiors and inferiors took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: The students bowed twice facing north, divided into the two corridors, and all took their seats.

sentences.zh: 賜茶畢，三公以下降階，學生自兩廡降階，北面再拜，群臣以次出。

translations.literal: When the granting of tea was finished, the Three Excellencies and below descended the steps; students descended from the two corridors, faced north and bowed twice; the various ministers withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: When tea had been served, the Three Excellencies and others descended the steps; students descended from the corridors, bowed twice facing north, and the ministers withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 上降坐還次，乘輦還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the seat, returned to the tent, rode the palanquin back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left his seat, returned to the tent, and rode back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 時命禮部侍郎秦熺執經、司業高閎講《易》之《泰》，遂幸養正、持志二齋，賜閌三品服，學官遷秩，諸生授官免舉，賜帛有差。

translations.literal: At the time he ordered Ministry of Rites Vice Director Qin Xi to hold the classic and Vice Director Gao Kan to lecture on the "Tai" hexagram of the Changes; he then visited the Yangzheng and Chizhi studios; granted Kan third-rank robes; school officials were promoted in rank; students were granted offices and exempted from examinations; silk was granted in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he appointed Ministry of Rites Vice Director Qin Xi to hold the classic and Vice Director Gao Kan to lecture on the "Tai" hexagram of the Changes, then visited the Yangzheng and Chizhi studios. Gao Kan received third-rank robes; school officials were promoted; students were appointed to office and exempted from examinations; and silk was granted in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 上既奠拜，注視貌象，翼翼欽慕，覽唐明皇及太祖、真宗、徽宗所製讚文，命有司悉取從祀諸讚，皆錄以進。

translations.literal: After the emperor had completed the libation and bows, he gazed attentively at the image, reverently admiring it; he reviewed the encomia composed by Tang Minghuang and Taizu, Zhenzong, and Huizong; he ordered the relevant offices to gather all encomia for collateral sacrifices and record them all to present.
translations.idiomatic: After completing the libation and bows, the emperor gazed reverently at the image and reviewed encomia composed by Tang Minghuang and by Taizu, Zhenzong, and Huizong. He ordered the relevant offices to gather all encomia for collateral sacrifices and submit them for the record.

sentences.zh: 帝遂作先聖及七十二子讚，冠以序文，親灑翰墨，以方載之，五月丙辰，登之彩殿，備儀衛作樂，命監學之臣，自行宮北門迎置學宮，揭之大成殿上及二廡。

translations.literal: The emperor then composed encomia for the Former Sage and the seventy-two disciples, prefixed with a preface; he personally applied brush and ink; they were mounted on square tablets; on the bingchen day of the fifth month, they were displayed in the Colored Hall with full guards of honor and music; he ordered the school-supervising officials to receive them from the northern gate of the traveling palace and install them in the school, posting them above the Dacheng Hall and in the two corridors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then composed encomia for the Former Sage and the seventy-two disciples, prefaced with his own brushwork, mounted on square tablets. On the bingchen day of the fifth month they were displayed in the Colored Hall with full ceremonial guards and music, then carried from the traveling palace's north gate to the academy and posted above the Dacheng Hall and in both corridors.

sentences.zh: 序曰：“朕自睦鄰息兵，首開學校。

translations.literal: The preface said: "Since I made peace with neighbors and ceased warfare, I have first opened schools.
translations.idiomatic: The preface read: "Since I made peace with our neighbors and ceased warfare, I have first opened schools.

sentences.zh: 教養多士，以遂忠良。

translations.literal: I nurture and teach many scholars, thereby bringing loyal and good men to fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: I nurture and teach many scholars to bring forth loyal and worthy men.

sentences.zh: 繼幸太學，延見諸生。

translations.literal: I then visited the Imperial Academy and received the various students.
translations.idiomatic: I then visited the Imperial Academy and received the students in audience.

sentences.zh: 濟濟在庭，意甚嘉之。

translations.literal: They filled the courtyard in abundance; my mind greatly approved them.
translations.idiomatic: They filled the courtyard in splendid array, and I was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 因作《文宣王讚》。

translations.literal: Therefore I composed the "Encomium for King Wenxuan."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I composed the "Encomium for King Wenxuan."

sentences.zh: 機政餘閑，曆取顏回而下七十二人，亦為製讚。

translations.literal: In the leisure left from state affairs, I took in turn Yan Hui and the seventy-two men below him and also composed encomia for them.
translations.idiomatic: In the leisure left from state affairs, I took in turn Yan Hui and the seventy-two disciples below him and composed encomia for each.

sentences.zh: 用廣列聖崇儒右文之聲，復知‘師弟子間纓弁森森、覃精繹思’之訓，其於世道人心庶幾焉。

translations.literal: By this I extend the reputation of successive sages who honored Confucian learning and valued literature; I also restore knowledge of the teaching that 'between teacher and disciples caps and gowns stand in dense ranks, deeply refining and elaborating thought'—perhaps thereby the ways of the age and the hearts of men may be somewhat improved.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I extend the reputation of successive sages who honored Confucian learning and valued literature, and restore the teaching that 'between teacher and disciples caps and gowns stand in dense ranks, deeply refining and elaborating thought'—perhaps thereby the ways of the age and the hearts of men may be somewhat improved.

sentences.zh: ”二十六年十二月，言者謂：“陛下崇儒重道，製為讚辭，刻宸翰於琬琰，光昭往古。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month of the twenty-sixth year, a memorialist said: "Your Majesty honors Confucian learning and esteems the Way, composing encomia and carving the imperial brush upon fine jade, illuminating past antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month of the twenty-sixth year a memorialist said: "Your Majesty honors Confucian learning and esteems the Way, composing encomia and carving your imperial brush upon fine stone to illuminate the past.

sentences.zh: 寰宇儒紳，敦不顧瞻《雲漢》之章？

translations.literal: Confucian gentry throughout the realm—how could they not gaze upon the "Milky Way" chapters?
translations.idiomatic: Confucian gentry throughout the realm—how could they fail to gaze upon these lofty compositions?

sentences.zh: 請奉石刻於國子監，以碑本遍賜郡學。

translations.literal: I request that stone inscriptions be installed at the Directorate of Education, and that rubbings of the steles be bestowed broadly on prefectural schools.
translations.idiomatic: I request that stone inscriptions be installed at the Directorate of Education and that rubbings be distributed to prefectural schools throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 淳熙四年，孝宗幸太學，如紹興之儀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunxi, Xiaozong visited the Imperial Academy, following the Shaoxing protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunxi, Xiaozong visited the Imperial Academy following the Shaoxing protocol.

sentences.zh: 命禮部侍郎李燾執經、祭酒林光朝講《大學》。

translations.literal: He ordered Ministry of Rites Vice Director Li Tao to hold the classic and Libationer Lin Guangchao to lecture on the Great Learning.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Ministry of Rites Vice Director Li Tao to hold the classic and Libationer Lin Guangchao to lecture on the Great Learning.

sentences.zh: 尋幸武學，如太學之儀。

translations.literal: Soon after he visited the Military Academy, following the Imperial Academy protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He soon visited the Military Academy following the same protocol as at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝肅揖武成王，不拜。

translations.literal: The emperor made a solemn bow to King Wucheng but did not perform the full prostration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made a solemn bow to King Wucheng but did not perform the full prostration.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年正月，寧宗幸太學，如淳熙之儀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jiatai, Ningzong visited the Imperial Academy, following the Chunxi protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Jiatai, Ningzong visited the Imperial Academy following the Chunxi protocol.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年正月，理宗幸太學，宗、武兩學官屬、生員並赴太學陪位，候車駕至學，詣先聖文宣王位，三上香，執爵三祭酒，俯伏，興，再拜，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Chunyou, Lizong visited the Imperial Academy; officials and students of the National University and Military Academy all went to the Imperial Academy to accompany in position; when the imperial carriage arrived at the school, he went to the position of the Former Sage King Wenxuan, thrice offered incense, held the goblet and thrice poured libation, prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice; all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Chunyou, Lizong visited the Imperial Academy. Officials and students of the National University and Military Academy all attended at the Imperial Academy. When the imperial carriage arrived, he went to the Former Sage King Wenxuan, offered incense three times, poured libation three times from the goblet, prostrated himself, rose, and bowed twice; all officials in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至崇化堂，宰臣、使相、執政並起居。

translations.literal: The emperor arrived at the Chonghua Hall; chief ministers, commissioners, and chief councilors all performed greetings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proceeded to the Chonghua Hall, where chief ministers, commissioners, and chief councilors all greeted him.

sentences.zh: 執經官由東階、講官由西階並升堂，於御前分東西相向立。

translations.literal: The classic-holder ascended by the eastern steps and the lecturer by the western steps; both ascended the hall and, before the emperor, divided east and west and stood facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: The classic-holder ascended by the eastern steps and the lecturer by the western, then stood before the emperor facing one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 次引國子監三學學官、學生一班北面再拜，讚各就坐，賜茶。

translations.literal: Next they led one formation of school officials and students of the three schools of the Directorate of Education; facing north they bowed twice; it was intoned that each should take his seat; tea was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Next one formation of school officials and students of the three schools bowed twice facing north, were announced to take their seats, and were granted tea.

sentences.zh: 俟講書畢，起，立班再拜。

translations.literal: When the lecture was finished, they rose, formed ranks, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture ended, they rose, formed ranks, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 禮成，執經官、講書官、國子監三學官、生員各推恩轉官有差。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the classic-holder, lecturers, school officials of the three schools of the Directorate of Education, and students each received grace promotions and transfers in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, the classic-holder, lecturers, school officials of the three schools, and students each received promotions and rewards in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 咸淳三年正月戊辰，度宗幸太學祗謁，禮部尚書陳宗禮執經，國子祭酒雷宜中講《中庸》，餘並如儀。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the first month of the third year of Xianchun, Duzong visited the Imperial Academy in reverent audience; Ministry of Rites Director Chen Zongli held the classic; National University Libationer Lei Yizhong lectured on the Doctrine of the Mean; the rest followed protocol.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the first month of the third year of Xianchun, Duzong visited the Imperial Academy in reverent audience. Ministry of Rites Director Chen Zongli held the classic and National University Libationer Lei Yizhong lectured on the Doctrine of the Mean; the rest followed protocol.

sentences.zh: 賜貢士宴，名曰“聞喜宴”。

translations.literal: Banquets were granted to presented scholars, named the "Hearing Joy Banquet."
translations.idiomatic: Banquets were granted to presented scholars, called the "Hearing Joy Banquet."

sentences.zh: 《政和新儀》：押宴官以下及釋褐貢士班首初入門，《正安之樂》作，至庭中望闕位立，樂止。

translations.literal: The Zhenghe New Protocols: the banquet presiding officials and below and the newly robed presented scholars' rank leader, on first entering the gate, the Zheng'an music was performed; arriving in the courtyard they stood facing the palace gate position; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenghe New Protocols: when the banquet presiding officials and the rank leader of the newly robed presented scholars first entered the gate, the Zheng'an music was performed; they halted in the courtyard facing the palace gate, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 預宴官就位，再拜訖。

translations.literal: The banquet participants took their positions and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The banquet participants took their positions and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 押宴官西向立，中使宣曰“有敕”，在位者皆再拜訖。

translations.literal: The presiding banquet official stood facing west; the palace envoy announced "There is an edict"; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The presiding banquet official stood facing west. The palace envoy announced "There is an edict," and all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 中使宣曰“賜卿等聞喜宴”，在位者皆再拜，搢笏，舞蹈，又再拜。

translations.literal: The palace envoy announced "I grant you the Hearing Joy Banquet"; all in attendance bowed twice, inserted their tablets, performed the dance, and bowed again twice.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy announced "I grant you the Hearing Joy Banquet." All present bowed twice, inserted their tablets, performed the dance, and bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 次引押宴官稍前謝坐再拜，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: Next they led the presiding banquet official slightly forward to thank for the seats and bow twice; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Next the presiding banquet official was led slightly forward to thank for the seats and bow twice; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 若賜敕書，即引貢士班首稍前，中使宣曰“有敕”，貢士再拜。

translations.literal: If an edict document was granted, they then led the presented scholars' rank leader slightly forward; the palace envoy announced "There is an edict"; the presented scholars bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: If an edict document was granted, the rank leader of the presented scholars was led slightly forward; the palace envoy announced "There is an edict," and the presented scholars bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 中使宣曰“賜卿等敕書”，班首稍前，搢笏，跪，中使授敕書訖，少退，班首以敕書加笏上，俯伏，興，歸位再拜，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The palace envoy announced "I grant you an edict document"; the rank leader stepped slightly forward, inserted his tablet, knelt; the palace envoy handed over the edict document and finished; he withdrew slightly; the rank leader placed the edict document atop his tablet, prostrated himself, rose, returned to position and bowed twice; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy announced "I grant you an edict document." The rank leader stepped forward, inserted his tablet, and knelt. The palace envoy handed over the document, then withdrew slightly. The rank leader placed the document atop his tablet, prostrated himself, rose, returned to position, and bowed twice; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 凡預宴官分東西升階就坐，貢士以齒。

translations.literal: All banquet participants ascended the steps east and west to take seats; presented scholars were seated by age.
translations.idiomatic: All banquet participants ascended the steps east and west to take their seats; presented scholars were seated by seniority.

sentences.zh: 酒初行，《賓興賢能之樂》作，飲訖、食畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When wine was first served, the "Guest-Rising Worthy Talent" music was performed; when drinking and eating were finished, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was first served, the "Guest-Rising Worthy Talent" music was performed; when drinking and eating were finished, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 酒再行，《於樂辟廱之樂》作。

translations.literal: When wine was served a second time, the "In Music at the Piyong" music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was served a second time, the "In Music at the Piyong" music was performed.

sentences.zh: 酒三行，《樂育人材之樂》作。

translations.literal: When wine was served a third time, the "Music Nurturing Human Talent" music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was served a third time, the "Music Nurturing Human Talent" music was performed.

sentences.zh: 酒四行，《樂且有儀之樂》作。

translations.literal: When wine was served a fourth time, the "Music and Moreover There Is Ritual" music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was served a fourth time, the "Music and Moreover There Is Ritual" music was performed.

sentences.zh: 酒五行，《正安》之樂作。

translations.literal: When wine was served a fifth time, the Zheng'an music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was served a fifth time, the Zheng'an music was performed.

sentences.zh: 再坐，酒行、樂作，節次如上儀。

translations.literal: They sat again; wine was served and music performed; the sequence followed the above protocol.
translations.idiomatic: They sat again; wine was served and music performed in the same sequence as above.

sentences.zh: 皆飲訖、食畢，樂止。

translations.literal: All finished drinking and eating; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: All finished drinking and eating, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 押宴官以下俱興，就次，賜花有差。

translations.literal: The presiding banquet officials and below all rose and went to their stations; flowers were granted in varying amounts.
